correctness.rationale: The affine recurrence was reconstructed from the zero of the affine operator. Its companion characteristic determinant is \(\det((r^2-r)I+\lambda(2r-1)M)\), so stability reduces to the scalar equation over spectral values of \(M\). Strong monotonicity and the norm bound imply the exact half-disk enclosure \(\operatorname{Re}\zeta\ge q\), \(|\zeta|\le1\). A fresh symbolic elimination of a unit-circle root reproduced \(c(t)=(5t^2-2)/(2(2t^2-1))\), \(\phi(t)=t(3t^2-1)/(2(1-2t^2))\), its strict increase on \([1/\sqrt3,2/3]\), and the cubic \(3t^3+4qt^2-t-2q=0\). The planar rotation-dilation has exactly the boundary spectral value, and the scalar endpoint gives the multiplier \(r=-1\). Finite-dimensional spectral radius below one is sufficient for R-linear convergence even for defective matrices.

correctness.rationale: The affine reflected-gradient recurrence reduces exactly to a quadratic characteristic equation for each eigenvalue of the operator matrix. Strong monotonicity and the spectral-norm bound give a half-disk spectral enclosure. Parameterizing a unit-modulus characteristic root, eliminating the angular variable, and enforcing both enclosure constraints yields the unique cubic threshold. Strict stability below it follows by continuity from small positive steps, and a two-dimensional normal rotation-dilation matrix attains the boundary. Symbolic checks verify the elimination, derivative, endpoints, representative contact, and numerical specialization.
